study.question: Observed in baseline-din: macro validation AUC 0.8099233881, macro Logloss 0.05662295138; its source retrieves one target-conditioned history summary without user/context conditioning before separate task towers. Empty/1-16/17-64/>64 history slice macro AUCs are 0.72684/0.76284/0.78929/0.82734. Slice prevalence and cohort differences prevent a causal bottleneck inference. Does allowing field interactions and history retrieval to alter one another across two reads improve the frozen four-task objective beyond matched fixed-query and fixed-event alternatives?
study.hypothesis: Provisional mechanism: the first history read updates field/task states, which can then both change the second retrieval query and write context back into individual event states. This reciprocal loop can recover task-relevant combinations that a fixed summary misses. The proposed test separates query evolution (A) and event feedback (B) using a 2x2 design. The observed code restriction motivates the question; neither the baseline metric nor the external references establish that this mechanism is useful locally.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary text, especially local target-conditioned activation, and baseline_reference.py were inspected. Retain field embeddings and four task towers but replace one local-activation read with explicit field/task tokens and two cross-attention reads; this is not an exact DIN reproduction.

Sections 3.1-3.3 describe mixed-parameter causal joint attention and sequence reduction. Here use alternating cross-attention without event-event attention or pruning, shared field transforms with identity offsets, and an explicit target-conditioned field-to-event write. No claim of priority or equivalent reproduction.

Pinned forward and OneTransBlock paths inspected (132-252). Used to check the joint-interaction precedent; no copied model blocks. Original causal behavior and this benchmark implementation must not be equated.

Section 5.3 uses non-behavioral queries over behavioral keys/values. Adopt the economical cross-interaction direction, but add an experimentally removable reverse write and use shared projections with field identities. No content features, CSA, extra candidate behavior retrieval or industrial caching are available here.

Sections 4.2-4.4 describe interleaved global/sequence learning with a summarizing bridge, personalized FFN and sequence MHA. Reciprocal exchange is established prior work. This local variant uses direct event-to-field and field-to-event cross-attention, no personalized FFN or event self-attention, and a factorial intervention on two feedback links. Novelty remains unverified.

study.proposed_difference: Represent each current target/user/context field as a 32-dimensional token plus four learned task tokens. Project each historical exposure with its item fields and authorized action into a 32-dimensional event token; add mask-derived valid-prefix rank. Mix fields once, read every valid event, mix fields, optionally write the resulting field states into each event, read again using either evolved or initial field queries, then mix fields and read four task heads. Keep all 100 available events; no event-event attention. All arms retain identical raw-field skip and log history count. A fixed zero null is enabled only for empty histories, and padded events are masked before projection and after writes. The A/B switches change information paths, not parameter allocation. Both-static has identical weight-tied retrieval at both reads, so any improvement over it requires an evolving query or event state rather than merely having an extra independent retrieval module.
predictions: Primary: exchange_full exceeds exchange_fixed_both in validation macro AUC; 0.001 absolute AUC is a predeclared practical target for prioritizing expensive follow-up, not a selection veto or significance threshold. Report all four per-task AUC/Logloss deltas against baseline-din and the closest control.

A effect with no B: AUC(read_only)-AUC(fixed_both). B effect with no A: AUC(fixed_query)-AUC(fixed_both). Conditional A effect: AUC(full)-AUC(fixed_query). Conditional B effect: AUC(full)-AUC(read_only). Compute interaction I=AUC(full)-AUC(read_only)-AUC(fixed_query)+AUC(fixed_both); a positive I motivates a synergy explanation, not proof from one seed.

The conditional effects should be more evident in the existing 17-64 and >64 history slices than empty histories if history ambiguity is the mechanism. These are predeclared contrasts; full-data cohort prevalence differences still confound between-slice comparisons. Always provide sample/positive/negative counts and mark rare-task slices preliminary.

At identical model weights, all four switch settings yield the same predictions for entirely empty histories: history evidence and event writes are zero. Separately trained models need not agree on empty-history samples.

Analytic attention cost has O(F*L*d + F*F*d), not O(L*L*d), for fixed two reads and one write, where F includes four task tokens. Only measured host wall time, inference latency and peak memory can establish a practical cost advantage.
falsifiers: If exchange_full fails to outperform the closest single-link control reproducibly, two-way feedback is not supported in this implementation even if all arms beat DIN.

If read_only matches or exceeds full, prefer the simpler one-way path and do not attribute gains to event feedback. If fixed_query matches or exceeds full, evolving retrieval queries are not supported.
An absent or negative factorial interaction contradicts a synergy claim; positive main effects without positive interaction support separable contributions only.
If all four variants underperform DIN on the fixed objective or exceed the host resource cap, reject this implementation as a candidate; this does not refute all unified interaction architectures.

If padded-ID changes, current-target action changes, or unrelated batch samples change an evaluation prediction, or empty histories yield nonfinite predictions/gradients, stop for an integrity or implementation fix before scoring. Those failures are not scientific counterevidence.
alternative_explanations: Changes from DIN simultaneously introduce softmax attention, token projection, position rank, LayerNorm, history count, raw skip and task tokens. DIN comparison is a whole-architecture quality/cost comparison; only the four matched variants isolate the feedback links.
History slice gaps can reflect label prevalence, user support, static-feature difficulty and cohort composition rather than lost sequence information.

Event writes can work as a context shortcut or extra nonlinear capacity rather than improved event selection. If B is consequential, reserve a replacement control using event-independent broadcast feedback, followed by key-only versus value-only feedback to discriminate this explanation.

Width 32 can discard within-event detail, and fixed one-pass training may favor faster-converging architectures. A null result can be undercapacity or optimization failure; use measured loss/gradient diagnostics to choose one discriminating follow-up rather than unstructured tuning.

One initialization cannot establish reproducibility. Repeated user exposures are dependent; use paired seeds and user-cluster bootstrap only if the host authorizes the necessary identity-aware output.

Official offline historical feedback can be immature at serving time; the auxiliary outcomes concern user/category/brand matches within 24h, not advertisement-specific conversion. No production causal claim is admissible.
